evidence: The training was conducted in the Kaggle environment utilizing a dual GPU T4 setup with 15 GiB of memory, using the Adam optimizer for fifteen epochs.
Each dataset was subsequently partitioned into training and testing subsets using an 80/20 split, respectively.
The analyzed configurations include: ResNet-1D, BiGRU-MHA, ResNet-1D-BiGRU, and ResNet-1D-BiGRU-MHA, with varying numbers of attention heads, dropout rates, and dense layers.
SMOTE was applied during training on the Edge-IIoTset dataset.
unresolved: n_models=10 counts the distinct architectural variants in the Table III ablation study (case #1-#10); the paper frames these as ablation configurations of one proposed model rather than separate baseline architectures, so a stricter reading could give n_models=1.
No random seed, repetition count, or run-to-run variability (std/CI) is reported anywhere; all metrics appear to be single-run point estimates.

n_eval_types=10 counts Accuracy, Loss, Precision, Recall, F1, FPR, inference time, training time/epoch, ROC/AUC, and confusion matrix; some of these (e.g. confusion matrix) are diagnostic displays rather than summary metrics, so a narrower count is defensible.
control_arm/significance_test fields are not really applicable since this is a plain multiclass-classification NIDS paper, not a backdoor/poisoning study; marked null/none accordingly.
